content: 1. Acitretin reduces the effectiveness of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism. This interaction is contraindicated as it may lead to contraceptive failure. Avoid coadministration. 2. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, as a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as per prescribing information. 3. Belzutifan reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with hormonal contraceptives may result in contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 4. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 5. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase menstruation-associated adverse effects, including amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 6. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 7. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 9. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 10. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 11. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may reduce systemic exposure to ethinyl estradiol and progestin, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during coadministration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 12. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 18. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 19. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase menstruation-associated adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 20. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates according to product labeling. 21. Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 22. Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate may mutually reduce each other's effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 23. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 24. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Hormonal contraceptive effectiveness may be diminished. Additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 25. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 26. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone acetate by weak-to-moderate induction of CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 27. Exenatide injectable solution may reduce the extent and rate of absorption of oral contraceptives due to its effect on slowing gastric emptying. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 28. Exenatide injectable suspension may similarly reduce the absorption of oral contraceptives. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 29. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 30. Iloperidone increases the levels of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 31. Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 32. Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 33. Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 34. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 35. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 36. Norethindrone acetate reduces the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 37. Norethindrone acetate increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. There is potential for increased toxicity. 38. Mifepristone reduces the effects of norethindrone acetate by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 39. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 40. Rufinamide decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rufinamide may decrease the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. 41. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated by infection and inflammation. Use caution if coadministered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 42. Stiripentol inhibits and induces CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially altering the effects of norethindrone acetate. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 43. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered.
